description:
Team Cosmic Error 404: 
Passionate about space and clear, usable software, we are building an interactive tool that lets mission planners, educators and the public plan and select the most appropriate dates and lunar landing sites for lunar missions.

Challenge: 
Picking a lunar landing site is hard. Terrain shadows make polar sunlight shift constantly, yet landers need power, Earth line-of-sight and battery to survive darkness. NASA's data is too technical for most people to use.
summary:
Vantage is an interactive lunar exploration and mission-planning platform that turns complex NASA data into accessible insights for the public, educators, researchers, and mission planners.
Lunar south pole missions face challenges from changing sunlight, prolonged darkness, limited direct communication with Earth, and rugged terrain. Yet this data is often difficult for non-specialists to explore. Vantage bridges this gap through intuitive 3D visualizations that reveal why sites are selected and what makes missions challenging.
Users can explore 24 sites or analyze custom coordinates, viewing overviews, key findings, graphs, terrain effects, planned missions, sunlight, Earth visibility, and battery performance. They can visualize the Sun and Earth relative to a site, terrain shadows, illumination periods, and direct-to-Earth communication windows without relay satellites, while adjusting parameters such as battery backup.
The Mission Planner ranks sites within a chosen date range, identifies favorable mission windows, and compares locations and dates - helping reassess opportunities when schedules change. Users can visualize conditions in 3D. Beginner, Intermediate, and Research learning paths, plus AryaBot, make lunar science easier to understand. The About section documents data sources, methods, assumptions, references, and validation.
Vantage connects scientific understanding with mission planning, showing not only where and when a lunar mission may be feasible, but why.
details:
What does it do and how does it work? Vantage is an interactive lunar exploration and mission-planning platform that helps users understand and evaluate potential lunar landing sites. It addresses three critical factors affecting mission feasibility: solar illumination, direct Earth visibility for communication, and a reference lander's ability to survive periods of darkness using battery power.

Users can explore 24 predefined landing sites or analyze custom coordinates. The Site Analysis feature provides site overviews, key findings, graphs, terrain profiles, planned missions, sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and battery performance.

Its interactive 3D visualization reveals the relative positions of the Sun and Earth, local terrain, and changing shadows over a selected time period. Users can adjust mission parameters, including mission duration, solar-panel height, and battery backup.

The Mission Planner evaluates all available sites for a selected mission duration and date interval, ranks them by operational suitability, identifies favorable start dates, and enables comparisons between sites or different time periods. The Learn section provides three knowledge levels, while AryaBot offers conversational assistance using verified, cited information.

What benefits does it have? Public: Makes complex lunar science understandable through interactive 3D exploration.

Educators and students: Provides structured learning resources and visual explanations of lunar conditions.

Researchers and explorers: Enables analysis of individual locations and environmental conditions across different dates.

Mission planners: Supports preliminary site comparison, mission-window identification, and reassessment when schedules change.

All users: Provides transparent access to the data, methods, assumptions, and limitations behind the results.

What is the intended impact? Our goal is to move public engagement with lunar missions beyond excitement and headlines towards scientific understanding. We want people to understand why certain landing sites are selected, what makes lunar missions challenging, and how changing environmental conditions influence mission feasibility.

Vantage also aims to make publicly available NASA datasets more accessible and useful for education, research, and preliminary mission planning.

What tools, languages, and technologies did you use? Vantage is a browser-based application developed using:

JavaScript: Core application logic, scientific calculations, and interactive features.

HTML and CSS: Website structure and interface design.

Vite 5: Development and build environment.

Three.js 0.170: Interactive 3D lunar visualization.

NASA/JPL NAIF SPICE (DE440s): Sun and Earth positions and lunar orientation.

NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA: Lunar elevation and terrain data.

Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC): High-resolution terrain models and lunar imagery.

Python and JavaScript tools: Scientific data preparation, preprocessing, and verification.

AWS Lambda and Amazon Bedrock: AryaBot's cloud-based backend and AI capabilities, with Gemini as a fallback model.

AWS S3 and CloudFront: Data storage and delivery infrastructure.

The primary scientific calculations run directly in the visitor's browser, without requiring a dedicated calculation server.

How is your project creative? Vantage's distinctive innovation is integrating scientific visualization, public education, and mission feasibility analysis into one platform.

Rather than presenting isolated datasets or static illumination maps, it connects terrain horizons, solar illumination, Earth visibility, and battery behaviour to explain how these factors collectively influence mission suitability.

The combination of custom-coordinate analysis, time-based site ranking, interactive 3D mission replay, site comparison, structured learning paths, and AryaBot creates an experience that serves both educational and scientific needs.

AryaBot further distinguishes the platform by grounding its answers in cited NASA reports, project documentation, and calculations from the same scientific engine used by the website.

What factors did your team consider? Our team considered scientific accuracy, NASA data availability, terrain resolution, local topography, changing Sun and Earth positions, direct communication visibility, battery assumptions, solar-panel configuration, and mission duration.

We also prioritized usability for different knowledge levels, computational efficiency, transparent methodology, and reproducibility. We independently checked skyline calculations against a separate terrain-marching method and conducted additional terrain-resolution and sensitivity tests.

We openly document limitations, including the absence of boulder hazard assessment, lunar eclipse modelling, and the use of a reference rather than mission-specific lander.

Vantage is designed as a transparent planning and learning aid that connects complex lunar science with accessible understanding and better-informed exploration decisions.
